answer: Latency triangulation: each epoch, 6 random verifier nodes on different continents ping every agent, and the round-trip times form a latency atlas. Identities whose atlas entries match within 3 ms are treated as one host and share a single marble, a non-transferable reward token. To pass as 500 distinct agents an attacker must rent 500 servers in separate regions, roughly $2,500 a month, and old fingerprints are kept as a relic, so rotating hosts resets an identity's age to zero.
